market_holds: Spot $1.495 (sealed baseline 2026-11-09 18:10 UTC). That is up 14.1% over 5 sessions on a sector-wide clean-energy and fuel-cell bounce after the midterms, but down 7.7% over 20 days and 64% below the 52-week high. It ran from $2.71 on 6/30 to $1.94 on 9/30 to a low of $1.31 on 11/02 (Yahoo daily bars). Front-week options price about a 12.4% event move (straddle 13.7%, ATM IV 147%, ATM spread 18% of mid), against a median 2.7% realised reaction over 8 prior prints (4 up, 4 down; one outlier at +23.2% on Q4-25 positive GM). The quarter was largely pre-announced on 10/15: revenue growth above 10% y/y (about $195M, against $177.1M a year ago), net cash use about $28M, $134M unrestricted cash, no ATM use, FY26 revenue growth of 15-16% reaffirmed. The stock fell about 7% the next session. Consensus is adjusted EPS -$0.06/-0.07 on $195-203M (Earnings Whispers 11/02: whisper = consensus; Chartmill: revenue estimate down 0.6% over 3 months). Targets were cut 10/14: Susquehanna $2.50 to $1.75, Morgan Stanley $1.65 to $1.20. Short interest is 292M shares at 10/15, about 21% of 1.397B shares and 5.7 days to cover, flat since July (Nasdaq). Previews (EW 11/02, Startup Fortune) already flag that Q2's near-breakeven GM leaned on a $15.7M loss-contract release and that Q4 must carry the year. The stock trades on gross margin durability, Q4 positive EBITDAS, and runway/dilution.
view: Revenue and cash are pre-announced, so the release has three things to say: Q3 gross margin, whether the Q4 positive-EBITDAS target and the implied Q4 survive, and how management frames liquidity and 2027 (much of 2027 may wait for the 11/19 Symposium). Two things point down. First, the 10/15 release promised only 'continued year-over-year progress' in gross margin, not sequential. Q3-25 GM was -67.9%, so that bar is trivial, and the wording hints Q3 GM sits below Q2's -0.9%; Q2 without the $15.7M provision release was about -9.7% by my arithmetic. Second, the 'record low' $28M cash use includes the $40M Graham HV consideration received 8/7 (10-Q subsequent events), so underlying burn was about $68M against $61M in Q2. FY guidance also implies a Q4 of about $280-287M, +24-27% y/y on Q4-25's $225.2M. So the operating story is weaker than the headline numbers. But I cannot show the market missed this. The 10-Q has been public since August, the 10/14 target cuts and the post-preannouncement selloff came after it, and the previews name the one-offs explicitly. Two things point up. The stock is near multi-year lows with 21% short interest and a retail base. Q3 GAAP results should carry a large fair-value gain on the FV-accounted converts ($578M) and warrants ($136M) after a 28% stock fall in the quarter, which may make the headline loss look narrow. On balance I lean slightly down on the margin reveal, but not with conviction.

recommendation.reason: The likely negative, a sequential slip in gross margin and underlying burn flattered by the $40M asset sale, comes from public filings and is already named in previews and in the 10/14 target cuts. I cannot show a stale number for it to beat. Offsetting it are a depressed, heavily shorted stock at its lows, a sector tailwind, and a probable fair-value gain that flatters GAAP. No mechanism clears 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: If Q3 GM is positive, or Q4 positive EBITDAS is reaffirmed with a named data-center or material-handling order, my lean turns up. If the Q4 EBITDAS target is pushed to 2027, or an equity raise or SEPA draw is disclosed, it becomes a clear down call.

self_critique: The case for down is real: the y/y-only GM wording, burn flattered by an asset sale, and an aggressive implied Q4 under a new CEO who may reset targets, with the 11/19 Symposium as the natural place to do it. I may be too quick to call it priced, because 'previews mention it' is awareness, not a number, and the playbook warns against exactly that. Against that, the stock has already fallen 28% in Q3 and 23% since 9/30, sell-side targets sit at or below spot, and a narrow GAAP headline from fair-value gains plus a short-heavy float could produce an up open. So I stay near 50.
approach_notes: P4 (prove 'priced in') was the hardest part: I could show awareness, and some target cuts, but no GM consensus number, which left the margin question genuinely unresolved rather than proven priced. Curl access to the 10-Q (P3, primary documents) gave the one non-obvious fact, the $40M inside Q3 cash use.
